Carla Mendes: Heads-up — SummitCare renewal packet needs an SLA one-pager. Ask: 30d + 90d uptime, p95 main latency, p99 appendix, brief incident bullets, fallback usage, and a clear example of how credits would be applied. Can eng + billing assemble?

Rajat Singh: I can pull telemetry. Which service & regions? Also want to know if we should include committed vs burst Dedicated windows.

Carla Mendes: Service id = sc-prod-text. Regions = us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 secondary. They have reserved Dedicated windows on weekends — include a note that reserved windows are excluded from standard credits.

Maya Chen: I'll draft the customer-facing paragraph and an FAQ: "How are credits calculated and applied?" Please include T&C text if BillingBot can fetch it.

Zoe Kim: I'll collect incidents. Quick note — there was a storage failover on 2027-07-08 that caused a short degraded window; I have the RCA link. Fallback routing used twice in last 90d for short failovers.

Rajat Singh: Running exports now. Command I'll use: ```
# 30d + 90d uptime and latency by region
curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/summary?service=sc-prod-text&period=90d&group=region" | jq .
```
I'll upload CSV + Grafana images to /shared/reports/summitcare/1912345679.

BillingBot: T&C snippet: "Credits are calculated pro-rata against the customer's monthly committed spend. Issuance of credits requires Redwood validation and will be applied as an adjustment to the next invoice." (contract sc-2026-210).

Rajat Singh: Uploaded metrics.csv and grafana_shot.png. Quick numbers: us-east-1 uptime_30d=99.935%, us-east-1 uptime_90d=99.914%, eu-west-1 uptime_90d=99.998%; p95_us-east-1=230ms; p99_us-east-1=640ms; fallback_count_90d=2.

Zoe Kim: Incident bullets (short): 2027-07-08 storage failover — 9m degraded, mitigated by failback and config patch; 2027-06-20 routing flap — <3m, auto-failover used. Both marked medium/low customer impact. RCA links saved in the folder.

Maya Chen: Draft paragraph uploaded. For credits example, use a $15,000 monthly commit and these tiers (customer-specific):
- >=99.96% = no credit
- 99.92% - 99.96% = 4% credit
- 99.5% - 99.92% = 9% credit
- <99.5% = 15% credit
Using observed 30d us-east-1 = 99.935% -> falls into 99.5-99.92? actually 99.935% is in 99.92-99.96, so 4% credit = $600. Show both regional and combined examples.

Carla Mendes: Nice. Add a worked global example too: combine weighted uptime across regions based on request volume (we have that split 82% us-east, 18% eu-west). Rajat, can you compute a weighted 30d uptime?

Rajat Singh: On it. Quick calc: weighted_30d = 0.82*99.935 + 0.18*99.998 = ~99.95% (rounded). That lands right at the >=99.96? actually ~99.95 -> falls into 99.92-99.96 -> 4% credit. I'll put the exact math in the slides.

Maya Chen: Timeline: internal review by tomorrow 10am PT, customer-ready packet by EOD tomorrow. Please upload: metrics CSV, grafana shots, incident bullets, legal T&C text, and one-pager draft.

Zoe Kim: Incident bullets + RCA links uploaded.

Rajat Singh: Metrics and visuals uploaded to /shared/reports/summitcare/1912345679. I included a small script snippet for reproducibility: ```
# compute weighted uptime from CSV
python -c "import csv;w=0;u=0;\nfor r in csv.DictReader(open('metrics.csv')):\n  w+=float(r['req_frac']); u+=float(r['uptime'])*float(r['req_frac']);\nprint(u/w)"
```

Carla Mendes: Great. Maya & BillingBot, please confirm legal language and customer phrasing before I run the internal review.

BillingBot: Confirmed T&C text uploaded to the folder.

Maya Chen: I'll do a quick pass on wording now and flag any legal harmonization.

Carla Mendes: Thanks team — ping here once final slides are ready. If anything blocks the timeline call it out now. :thumbsup:
